title: Docs Site Runbook: Publishing, SDK Guides, and Canonical Support Fixes
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose:
This runbook consolidates operations and editorial procedures for the Redwood developer documentation site (docs.redwood.ai), with a focus on: SDK guide publication, quickstart/template lifecycle, API example validation, Site CI/CD, and the canonical fixes for the top support issues we see from customers. Use this page as the single source for day-to-day site ops for the DX team and on-call engineers.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: DX engineers, technical writers, on-call eng for docs site incidents, solutions engineers publishing examples.
- Scope: procedures for authoring, validating, publishing, rolling back docs; CI/CD and release checks; canonical fixes for frequent support tickets; monitoring and KPI thresholds.

Owner and escalation:
- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience docs team (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Secondary owner: eng-sre (pager: #eng-sre).
- Escalation path: docs on-call -> SRE on-call -> Head of DX -> Product (if content change impacts contracts/SLA).

Operating hours and SLA:
- Publishing window: 08:00–20:00 PDT weekdays for non-emergency content changes.
- Emergency fixes: 24/7 (use on-call).
- Target publish success rate: 99% (measured monthly).

Repository and deployment overview:
- Docs repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/docs-site.git (main branch protected).
- CI provider: GitHub Actions (docs-ci).
- Static site generator: Hugo + custom shortcodes and the DX theme.
- CDN: Cloudfront in front of S3 bucket (origin).
- Preview environments: Pull-request preview via netlify-preview (per-PR).

Pre-publish checklist (authors):
1) Lint and link-check: run local script `scripts/validate.sh` (see below).
2) API examples: run the example suite against staging API credentials and ensure no flaky tests.
3) SDK snippets: run unit smoke test: `python -m pytest tests/snippets` or `yarn test:snippets`.
4) Accessibility quickscan: `axe` browser extension or `npm run a11y-check` for pages with interactive components.
5) Metadata: frontmatter contains title, summary, tags, stable-url, and last_updated.

Local validation commands (examples):
```bash
# run static checks
./scripts/validate.sh
# run snippet tests (python SDK)
REDWOOD_API_KEY=$STAGING_KEY pytest tests/snippets/test_py_snippets.py -q
# run linkcheck
hugo --gc --minify && ./scripts/linkcheck.sh public
```

Publishing procedure (major doc or SDK guide):
1) Create a PR against `main` with descriptive title and change summary.
2) Assign reviewers from the reviewers list and any area owner (sdk-guides / product docs).
3) CI runs: lint -> snippet tests -> accessibility -> preview deploy.
4) Reviewer checklist (must be completed before merge):
   - Verify code examples execute against staging API and produce expected responses.
   - Confirm accuracy of SLOs, thresholds, and service names.
   - Validate wording for customer-facing clarity.
5) Merge by a reviewer (no self-merge for public-facing pages).
6) Post-merge: monitor the publish pipeline and CDN invalidation logs.

Rollback procedure (site or page-level):
1) If preview tests fail before merge: fix in branch.
2) If post-merge regression is detected: open an emergency PR reverting the merge and set PR title with `[EMERGENCY-ROLLBACK]` prefix.
3) SRE to coordinate cache invalidation and ensure the S3 origin matches the rollback commit.
4) Run smoke checks from multiple regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1).

Post-publish verification (10–15 min after merge):
- Check preview and live URL respond (curl + check status 200).
  `curl -sS -I https://docs.redwood.ai/path | grep HTTP`
- Validate snippet output with `scripts/verify_live_snippets.sh` (compares golden outputs).
- Confirm CDN invalidation completed in CloudFront console.
- Spot-check three pages for formatting on mobile and desktop.

Template for SDK guide (required frontmatter):
- required frontmatter keys: title, description, stable_url, sdk (python|js|go), sdk_version, tags, last_updated
- Example frontmatter: `---
title: "Quickstart: Python SDK v2"
sdk: python
sdk_version: "2.1.0"
---`

Canonical structure for an SDK guide page:
1) Short intro (1–2 paragraphs).
2) Installation snippet.
3) Minimal example with expected output.
4) Common pitfalls and troubleshooting (short bullets).
5) API reference link and changelog notes.
6) Test snippet that can be executed by CI.

API example validation checklist:
- Do examples use stable model names and deterministic seeds where applicable?
- Are environment variables (like REDWOOD_API_KEY) referenced but not leaked?
- Are examples idempotent and safe to run against staging?
- Do examples contain timeouts and retries for network calls?

Top support issues and canonical fixes (current list):
1) Auth failures in examples (most common)
   - Symptom: 401 when running snippets locally.
   - Root cause: author used personal dev key in repo or example references `REDWOOD_API_KEY` but user didn't set it.
   - Canonical fix: Add a clear auth setup section to every SDK guide and include `export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<YOUR_KEY>"` in examples; update `scripts/validate.sh` to detect hard-coded keys.
2) Streaming responses hang in previews
   - Symptom: Netlify preview shows spinner indefinitely for streaming examples.
   - Root cause: preview environment blocks WebSocket/stream upgrades or the preview proxy strips `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` headers.
   - Canonical fix: Add a fallback non-streaming example and a note in streaming docs explaining preview limitations. File a ticket to SRE to whitelist preview origin if long-term requirement.
3) Mismatched SDK version in snippets
   - Symptom: code uses `client.chat.stream()` which exists only in SDK v3 but page frontmatter claims v2.
   - Root cause: stale copy/paste across versions.
   - Canonical fix: Require `sdk_version` in frontmatter and add CI step to check snippet compatibility against that version by running `npx test-snippets --sdk-version $sdk_version`.
4) Broken links to product pages after model name changes
   - Symptom: 404s to model catalog links in older guides.
   - Canonical fix: Use stable redirectable paths (`/models/{slug}`) instead of raw model names, and add a weekly linkcheck job.

Monitoring, alerts and KPIs:
- Pager triggers: Site 5xx rate > 1% for 5m, Preview deploy failures > 3 in 1 hour.
- Dashboards to check: docs-build-failure-rate, docs-traffic-by-region, snippet-test-failures (per-sdk).
- Monthly KPI: snippet test pass rate >= 98%.

Runbook: common remediation commands and snippets:
- Re-run failed job locally: `GITHUB_ACTIONS=false ./scripts/ci-run.sh --job publish`
- Force CDN invalidation: `aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id E12345 --paths "/\*"`
- Rebuild preview manually: `./scripts/trigger-preview.sh <pr-number>`

Editorial notes and best practices:
- Keep examples minimal and copy-paste friendly (max 40 lines for a runnable snippet).
- Prefer explicit numeric examples for latency/cost where relevant (`Estimated cost: ~$0.002 per 1k tokens`).
- When documenting SLOs or thresholds, cite service names and owners (e.g., `Serving Runtime (owner: infra/runtime-team) - p99 latency < 350ms`).

Incident debriefs and postmortems:
- For any publish outage > 30 minutes open a postmortem in `confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/postmortems`.
- Include root cause, timeline, impacted pages, and the canonical fix applied.

Appendix: quick links and useful commands:
- Repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/docs-site.git
- CI status: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs-site/actions
- Preview checks: `./scripts/verify_preview.sh <preview-url>`

If you find gaps in this runbook or new recurring issues, add a short section under "Top support issues" and notify reviewers. This document is reviewed quarterly by the DX owner (owner: Aisha Patel).
